scene makikyoto1
Hello alone.
scene makikyoto2
So I’m here again, hello — on the way to wherever Maki wants to take me to try and fix me.
And while I’m ever-depressed by the notion that my misery is so apparent to everyone at this point, I take solace in the fact that this flaw has once again rescued me from harm’s way.
How lucky I am to have so many attentive friends. How lucky I am to be pulled away from my inner struggles constantly whenever they’re around.
It’s almost as if the world is telling me I’m not meant to be alone. Or that I should lean on others for help more. Or whatever else I know to be true but neglect to believe regardless.
She won’t force me to talk. She’ll merely give me the opportunity to. And should I neglect that as well, I imagine she’ll be perfectly content with just being in the same place as me.
Maybe she does just want to drive? That’s what I’ll tell myself until we get to wherever we’re going.
But when these shaking hands reach for the handle once this car comes to a stop, I pray that I won’t recall the days when they were smaller and steadier.
Someone else sat beside me back then.
Someone who I never thought I’d be able to live without.
How apt that I’ve spent nearly a decade since then coming to terms with (or avoiding) just how true that is.
: Have you ever driven a car, Akira?
: What?
scene makikyoto3
: Have you or have you not ever driven a motor vehicle? It’s a simple question.
: Oh, you’re not taking me somewhere I can “practice,” are you? You know I have a thing with cars.
: I’m not taking you anywhere in particular. I’m just driving.
scene makikyoto4
: We’re lucky to live somewhere we don’t really need to know how to drive. So it’s not every day you get to spend time without someone who has.
: It’s pretty liberating, actually. Terrifying, at first...but really freeing once the jitters wear off.
: Yeah...
: There are a lot of things in life like that, aren’t there?
scene makikyoto5
: Yeah...
: There sure are.
: You know...
: I’d never think less of someone for learning early. I’d think less of the person who taught them.

: Like Makoto, for example. I don’t think she’s ready yet, but I’ve told her about it and think she could figure it out pretty easily if she wanted to. Miku, though? I wouldn’t trust her behind the wheel of a car at all.
: The unfortunate truth, though, is that I wouldn’t be able to stop them if they really wanted to.
: That said, I’m not going to just hop in the passenger seat and watch as they figure it out on their own. Doing that would be directly putting them in harm’s way. Don’t you think?
: Maki-
: It’s just driving, Akira.
: We’re talking about driving.
: I’m sorry.
: I thought that would make it easier.
: There’s nothing to be sorry for.
: I just...
: Have a thing with cars.
scene makikyoto6
: Yeah...
: Why don’t we pull over then? This looks like a nice spot to get out and relax for a little while.
scene black
: Yeah...whatever you want.
Maki pulls off to the side of the road and parks her car in a spot with faded lines and cracked paint — causing memories to roll in before my shaking hands have the chance to evoke them.
scene clearnightsky
There was a spot that she used to park her car in after picking me up from Niki’s place.
Halfway between my childhood home and the one she made with him, there was an old shopping plaza she told me she worked at when she was younger.
I never believed her, though. The thought of her having any sort of regular job just seemed flat out bizarre to me. She was larger than life. She was Sekai.
Something didn’t always happen when she pulled into that spot in the back of the shopping plaza...But many days, something did.
Something that, like driving, felt liberating. Terrifying at first...but freeing once the jitters wore off.
She taught me everything I know.
Now, every single vehicle I lay my eyes on reminds me of her.
scene makikyoto7
Some days, when I stare up at that wall, I imagine what she would have done about it. Because if anyone could figure out how to scale it, it would have been her.

She didn’t even like sitting in that car for more than an hour at a time. She always needed to be moving. There’s no way she’d just sit back and let some colossal barrier keep her from getting out of here.
Guess she figured it out in the end, though. Now, even death can’t keep her in one place.
: It’s always crazy when I remember how we used to be able to just...leave. The thought of that today is just...surreal.
: Have you ever been outside of Kumon-mi?
: Kyoto for a field trip once.
: Ahh...
: Never been.
: It’s beautiful. Romantic. You’d love it there.
: Yeah...I probably would.
: Have you ever been anywhere outside of Kumon-mi? Tokyo, maybe?
: If I have, I can’t remember it.
: At the very least, I know Ami’s never left. No real desire to either.
: Yeah. Plenty of people seem perfectly content with just...never getting out and exploring.
: That was weird to me when I was younger, but I’m starting to understand it now.
: The longer we stay behind this thing, the more comfortable we become with everything that’s inside of it. But of course that makes everything on the outside scarier.
: Like, for all we know, everything else could be gone already.
: We still get TV and stuff from the outside, though.
: Sure, but is anything actually real before we see it with our own eyes?
: Yes. Otherwise those things would not exist for us to see. But I get what you’re saying.
: Yeah. Exactly. You’re the smart one here. I make a living selling rubber penises.
: You’re smart too, Maki. Your knowledge is just a little less...conventional than it is for most people.
: Thanks, Akira. That means a lot coming from someone who’s never bought any of my rubber penises.
: I will eventually. I still owe several people secret Santa presents, I think. Maybe I’ll just wait a few more years and place a bulk order?
: Well, you best hurry up or Miku’s Cock Emporium is going to put my place out of business.
: Only a matter of time.
: Only a matter of time...
scene makikyoto8
: I wonder if anybody’s ever had sex up against the barrier?
: Maki.
scene makikyoto9
: What?! That’s a totally normal thing to wonder! Somebody’s had to have done it by now, right?
: It...does seem statistically improbable that everyone in this city would have avoided it, yes.
scene makikyoto10
: I wonder what the first couple thought? Assuming it was a regular couple and not an orgy, of course. But hey, that sex club downtown organizes some crazy events sometimes. Maybe they did it?
: I’m sure learning a lot about a sex club I didn’t know existed until today...today.
if makisex == True:
: Maybe we can go together? You’ll get in for free if I bring you along.
: Only if you promise to stay mine while we’re in there and not run off with some other guy.
scene makikyoto11
: Deal.
: How about you, though? You’ll be immensely outnumbered. Think I’ll be enough for you in there?
: I think...I’m not sure if you want to be enough for me in there.
: Monogamy can be fun too, Akira.
scene makikyoto12
: Though...I guess it might be a little weird if we just go there and only screw each other. Nobody else there really rolls like that.
else:
: Great news for me. Less competition when it comes to buying their old stuff.
: You should check it out, though. You’d like it there. Plus, you’d be greatly outnumbered. Just one more benefit of not getting called to war and killed by aliens.
: Maybe the alien sex was worth it?
: Asking myself that question is exactly what I do to calm down when I think about Masahiro. He always said he wanted to fuck an alien.
scene makikyoto13
: Regardless, it’s cool knowing that, in this world of infinite possibilities, there are new “firsts” every single day.
: First people to bone up against the barrier...first people to talk about the first people to bone up against the barrier...and the first people to mention people talking about the first people to-
: I get it, Maki.
: Good, because I was starting to lose track of what I was saying.
scene makikyoto14
: But I guess if we’re all out of topics, we-
scene makikyoto15
: ...Akira?
scene black
scene makikyoto16
: Was...it something I said? Do you...need something? What do I-
: I should have gone...
: Gone...where?
: It doesn’t matter anymore...
: None of us are ever leaving this place again.
: D...Do I...hug you? Do I give you space? What do I do? I’m bad at this. You need to tell me or I’ll get it wrong.
scene makikyoto17
: Gah! My poor ghost legs! I’m never running that far again...especially in that white dress. It was so tight that I had no choice but to stop for a change of clothes on the way here.
scene makikyoto18
: So! What’d I miss? Anything fun? Anything sexy? What are you guys talking about?
: Nothing...
: Do...nothing? Okay. Got it. Carry on.
: No...not you, Maki.
: But...we’re the only ones here?
: Not to me, we’re not.
scene makikyoto19
: I...don’t think I...understand...
: Driving...
: I’m talking about driving.
scene makikyoto20
: Okay...sure.
: Was young.
: Very young...
scene makikyoto21
: But I loved that person...with every fiber of my being. And when she...
: When she died, it changed everything.
: I still see her, Maki.
: She follows me. She speaks to me. She-
: And she’s here right now?
: Present!
: Yeah...
: Can she hear me?
: Loud and clear!
: Yes...
: Great. Then can I have a minute to think of something really horrible to say to whoever did this to you?
scene makikyoto22
: One more girl who just doesn’t get it. We really are a rare breed nowadays.
: It wasn’t her fault. She really did love me. She just didn’t...see the world the way other people do.
: Akira-
scene makikyoto23
: I get it. I blame her too sometimes. But then I...
: I remember all the good things. How she saved me. How she gave me something I could finally look forward to in a world where I...never had anything like that.
scene makikyoto24
: So yeah...I gave her all of me. Or whatever I had left, I guess. And I don’t regret it at all, but...I’m a monster now.
: And I spend a lot of time just wishing I was someone else...or somewhere else.
: Anywhere but here would be fine.
: Anyone but me would be fine...
scene makikyoto25
: Your past doesn’t make you a monster, Akira.
: No, it doesn’t. But she painted everything black and it’s hard to just...paint over that because it feels like I’d be erasing her.
: And if I let go of the parts of myself that she put there...what if I never saw her again? Because I want to let go! I do...
: But I also don’t want her to stay gone forever. Because of those good parts. Because I loved her.
: That wasn’t love, Akira...That was-
scene makikyoto26
: No! You don’t get it! It was! And I know how it sounds, but it wasn’t like that! She was amazing! She wasn’t like me! I’m the one who’s terrible! She was just misunderstood!
: Aki-kun, don’t yell. She’s not going to get it. She’s not like us. Just let her say whatever she wants to say about me and call it a day. I can assure you I’ve heard worse.
: You’re not like that deplorable woman, Akira! I know you! You’re better than-
: You know what I want you to know! But what if there’s more to me than that?! What if I’ve been hiding something?! Then what?!
: Aki-kun, don’t do it. Don’t tell her you’ve-
scene makikyoto27
: Fucked your daughter like a gazillion times! Both daughters, actually! And guess what, lady?! All that time teaching them about safe sex was for nothing! My Aki-kun likes it raw!
scene makikyoto28
: Wha- get out of here, me! Aki-kun doesn’t want you here right now!
: Aki-kun doesn’t know what he wants! That’s why I’m here in the first place!
scene makikyoto29
: Aki-kun, look at me. You’re better than this. Don’t throw this away just because you’re getting emotional. It’s not worth it.
scene makikyoto30
: No, Aki-kun! Look at me! You’re not better than this. But that’s okay! We know who we are and hiding it won’t do anything but confuse us! Accept it and just live!
: Akira-
scene makikyoto31
: I don’t know what to do. I don’t know what to do. I don’t know what to-
: AKIRA!!!!
scene makikyoto32
scene makikyoto33
: Whatever you are...whatever you’ve done...it’s okay...
: We all make mistakes. But that doesn’t mean we can’t be forgiven.
: Can everything be forgiven, Maki?...You don’t know what I’ve done.
: That doesn’t matter. What matters is that you understand that what you’ve done is wrong and that you’re making an effort to get better.
: Hating you for being a shitty driver when you were taught by a shitty teacher isn’t going to do any good for anyone.
: What if I’m not trying to get better, though?...What if I’m barreling down some suburban street at twice the recommended speed with my eyes closed and my hands off the wheel?
: Then yeah, you’re a shitty person. But a shitty person wouldn’t be this-
: Broken?...
: Is that what you want to say?...
scene makikyoto34
: That changes nothing, Maki.
: I make my own decisions.
: Are you sure about that? Because I’m not sure I believe it if you’re hallucinating a dead woman, Akira.
: It gets...complicated when you...start bringing that kind of stuff into the picture. There’s all sorts of weird supernatural shit happening here every single day.
: That sounds exactly like what someone who’s losing it would say.
: Maki-
scene makikyoto35
: Makoto was the same way when Masahiro died. And I know you lost someone else not too long ago, so maybe you just need a reset?
: Heh...yeah. Because those fix everything.
: A little break won’t hurt you, will it?
: Maki, why do you think I haven’t gone back to school yet? Why do you think I spend my days just wandering around Kumon-mi looking for shit to do or people to kill time with?
: Because...
scene makikyoto36
: Because you’re lost...
: Bingo.
: How are we supposed to find where you’re meant to be then?
: You’re not supposed to do anything. I’m an adult. I’m supposed to figure that out alone. Like you did with Makoto.
: You helped me with Makoto. I owe it to you to at least try and do the same.
: Well...good luck. You’ve got your work cut out for you. Prepare to be let down more than you could ever believe.
: At the very least...
scene makikyoto37
: Thank you for telling me, Akira.
: Anything to lessen a burden placed entirely on you.
: This lessens nothing...just makes me more self-conscious around you.
: I’m sorry you feel that way, but I don’t. And if you ever need anything-
: Can I get a ride home? I want to see Ami.
scene black
: ...Yeah.
: And I want to see Makoto.
My hands are surprisingly still when I get back into Maki’s car, but I don’t understand why.
I feel no better than I did before. My chest is no lighter now that one more secret has been shed from it into the palms of someone else who cares for no good reason at all.
Despite this, though...and despite the many hints of my deranged depravity that I forced upon Maki just minutes ago...she never stops checking on me the whole way home.
I don’t understand why.
Is this willful ignorance?
Is it pity?
Or have I effortlessly warped her definition of “love” now too?
Whatever the case, there’s one thing I know for sure.
It’s that I fucking hate driving.
